newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon sets T$5 dividend and lower targets.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon sets T$5 dividend and lower targets.

text.p: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, Taiwan's largest semiconductor maker, said on Wednesday it has set lower net profit and sales targets for 1997 and a T$5/per share stock dividend for 1996.
Its board meeting has passed the dividend proposal, which would be slated for approval by the firm's shareholders' meeting to be held on May 13, the company said in a statement.
It set a 1997 net profit target at T$9.14 billion, down 52.9 percent from its actual 1996 net of T$19.4 billion, the statement said.
It set a 1997 sales target at T$35.22 billion, down 10.6 percent from its actual 1996 sales of T$39.4 billion.
Taiwan Semiconductor attributed the lower targets to the integrated circuits foundry market facing over-supply.

"With more and more companies entering the IC foundry business, the market for foundry production is facing over-supply and price deterioration," it said. "Nevertheless, our management considers that in the long run, there is still plenty of room for the company to grow."
The company is the world's largest IC foundry maker and many other firms followed in its path because of its success, it said.
The firm's foundry business is not based on the design and sale of its own IC products, but makes ICs according to others' orders.
